newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks give back most gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks give back most gains at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered most early gains at the close Tuesday but were seen keeping a strong tone despite a 25-basis points rise in the U.S. Federal Funds rate, dealers said.

"The market pulled back from its highs as a mere technical reaction after several days of gains, but the Federal Reserve's decision to hike rates won't make it switch course because it had already been discounted," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a session high of 751 and closed at 744.46 with a gain of 0.3 percent.
It had jumped 1.6 percent Monday and 2.6 percent last week, recovering from a slide earlier in March induced by the U.S. rate jitters.

"The bolsa held up well considering the U.S. long bond yield jumped to 6.97 percent from 6.89 percent after the rate announcement," another trader said. "The New York markets are just taking profits, and although we could see volatility there for a day or two more, we don't expect much action Wednesday on the bolsa."
Buenos Aires stock and bond markets close Thursday and Friday for the local Easter holidays.
"I suspect the bolsa will push moderately higher near-term, with some likely gyrations, and buyers will be selective," said Napoli. His choice picks were steel, construction and energy sector stocks.
Floor volume swelled to 29 million pesos in the session from 20.3 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover eased to 172.4 million pesos from 197.4 million Monday.
The broad market index inched up 0.1 percent, with winners beating losers 40 to 12 and 17 stocks closing flat.
Strongest main-tier gainers were oil company Astra, which rallied 3.1 percent, and holding company Comercial del Plata and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, both up 1.6 percent.
MerVal losers were led by construction stock Polledo and foods giant Molinos, down 1.8 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.
